Roster = clothing ITEMS (shirt, pants, …) rendered as the GARMENT ALONE on the stage (no body unless a try-on lens is explicitly added later). Reuse the source kit (store/panel/live/source/Stage pattern). Parity-capture discipline against the current clothing surface so nothing silently drops. THE FIX (ordered by the supervisor for you): one field per row, or 2-across max with real spacing; labels never colliding; fields grouped under their section headers honoring the conditional-sections law (SCULPTKIT-0606: render sections conditionally, not always). Dense is fine; OVERLAPPING is not.
Where: the layout lives in the ONE field renderer — `cart/hmsc-int/shell/fields.tsx` `PanelGroups`/`FieldCell` + the `C.FieldStrip`/`C.Field` classes in `cart/hmsc-int/shell/workbench.cls.ts` (FieldStrip is a wrapping row; that wrap at 290px with 34 num fields is the collision source). Constraint: fields.tsx is THE shared renderer — fix the layout for EVERY panel without forking it (a per-row strip variant or a width rule on `num` cells; check what the character/buildings panels look like after, they share the renderer). The settings panel generator (`editors/workbench/settings/panel.ts settingsPanel`) groups by owning route — 'paint' has 34 knobs in one group; consider sub-grouping by the table's top-level key (e.g. `brush.*`, `orbit.*`) which the registry's dotted paths give you for free. 2. THE KEY FACT (verified): `buildClothing(style, shapeId, pose, phase, actions, clothingSkin, accessories, bottoms, bonesOverride?) → ClothingInstance[]` in `game/figure/clothing.ts:29` is PURE and returns standalone garment primitives `{geometry: 'box'|'sphere'|'cone'|'cylinder', params, position, rotation, scale, color, opacity, textureKey}`. A garment renders BODILESS by mounting only these instances as `<Scene3D.Mesh>` nodes (geometry via `Geometry.GEOMETRIES[name]`-style mapping — see how DressedStage or `game/figure/render` maps ClothingInstance geometry strings; ObjectInspect3D.tsx:151 shows the `Geometry.GEOMETRIES[p.geometry] ?? Geometry.Box` idiom). Bottoms-only items: `buildClothing` builds top+bottoms together — check whether instances are separable (top vs bottoms) by reading the function body; if not separable, render with the top forced to 'underwear' to isolate bottoms, or add a pure helper in clothing.ts (additive) that returns instances tagged by garment slot. Do NOT fork the placement math — one truth.

3. ROSTER = the clothing items: 6 tops from `CLOTHING`, 5 bottoms from `BOTTOMS`, 4 accessories from `CLOTHING_ACCESSORIES` (group ids like `top:tee`, `bottom:jeans`, `acc:cap`). Roster rows can carry kind in the label; the items ARE the registry tables (P2 data) — generated, never enumerated by hand.

4. VARIANTS: a variant = the garment × a material/skin. Two layers, one truth:
   - The 5 built-in `CLOTHING_SKINS` (prints; textureKey `headlab.clothing.<skin>` via `clothingSkinTextureKey`) are seed variants.
   - USER variants = a material assignment from THE texture registry (`game/textures/registry.tsx` `allTextures`/`textureById`) picked through the `pick` field (`shell/fields.tsx` + `shell/picker.tsx` — the BUILDSKIN chooser; the dispatch explicitly requires the SAME chooser). Render a material variant by mounting `TextureCapture` (registry.tsx:133, staticKey convention like `clothvar:<id>`) and setting textureKey on the garment instances that carry the print today (buildClothing applies textureKey to print-bearing faces — check which instances get it and override there; you may need a textureKey override parameter or post-map the returned instances, post-mapping is fine since textureKey is plain data on the instance).
   - PERSISTENCE for user variants: a V20 stream the CLOTHSPLIT context owns. Check `game/figure/stream.ts` (charactersStream) for whether a clothing-variant event fits by ADDITION (the V20 law); if not, add a small `clothingStream` in `editors/` or extend charactersStream with a new event kind. Variants are {garmentId, variantId, label, material: textureKey | skin: ClothingSkinId}. Mirror the buildings suite trick: fake session folds through the REAL stream apply.
   - The VARIANT ROW/GRID: display in column 4 as a selectable strip under the garment view (selection = view state; LAW 1 — variant CREATION/assignment lives in gutter 3 via pick fields; clicking a variant in the stage SELECTS it, the WBCHAR C3 precedent).

5. STAGE: garment alone, orbit camera (copy the buildings Stage camera wire — ObjectInspect3D engage + setInputDeltas at lines ~130-200 of `editors/workbench/buildings/Stage.tsx`), the stage-kit lighting VERBATIM (`<Scene3D.Fog enabled={false}/>` + AmbientLight 0.55 + DirectionalLight direction=[0.5,1,0.35] intensity 0.95 + backgroundColor accentFor('bgElevated')) — the user already FAILED a stage for darkness once (req_0184); do not repeat it. Variant grid as a bottom band.

6. Read WBCLOTH.CAPTURE.md and decide row by row; never silently drop.

   `./tools/esbuild "$PWD/cart/hmsc-int/editors/workbench/clothing/clothing.test.ts" --bundle --outfile=zig-out/game/tests/wb_clothing.test.js --format=iife --platform=neutral --target=es2022 --alias:@reactjit=$PWD/runtime --alias:@game=$PWD/cart/hmsc-int/game --log-level=warning && ./tools/v8cli zig-out/game/tests/wb_clothing.test.js`

8. REGISTER in `editors/workbench/sources.ts` (re-read it fresh first — parallel lanes edit it). Decide with the capture whether the new source REPLACES clothingSource() in the registry (the fold: it must carry or account for everything) or coexists until the user passes it — match what BUILDSKIN did: replace only if every W-row is accounted; otherwise coexist and say so.

## Constraints, conventions, and gotchas

- HARD: no subagents/Task/Explore. No `git add -A`. MAIN only. DO NOT COMMIT — the supervisor sequences. Stage nothing.
- Dying routes/files are UNTOUCHED until flips; everything lands additively.
- The three chrome laws (WORKBENCH.md §1): col 3 edits / col 4 demonstrates (stage input = selection + camera only); lenses-only in the bar; no dead space. A "try-on" body view is OUT OF SCOPE unless added as an explicit LENS later — dispatch says garment alone.
- One source of truth: material = textureKey into game/textures registry; the chip-wall mistake (req_0184) is already fixed by `pick` — never inline a registry as enum opts.
- Headless test law: tests import store.ts/panel.ts only, never *.tsx. Test runner can't use Date.now in WORKFLOW scripts but CAN in v8cli tests (smooth.test precedent).
- `tools/request`: supervisor dispatches are marker-tracked (no ledger resolve needed); if the USER prompts you directly without a capture line, `tools/request log` FIRST, verbatim.
- Build verification: never run node/bun; esbuild + v8cli only; the user runs the dev loop (auto-push watcher) — don't run `rjit dev`.
- `rjit shot` rebuilds via ship when the binary is stale; pre-ship with SHIP_RUN_PACKAGE=0 for speed; flock serializes with other lanes — just let it queue.
- fields.tsx is shared and hot (another lane reshaped SliderField this session) — re-read before editing; your additions must be additive.
- The user judges by outcome. The PASS for this task: open /workbench → the clothing source shows SHIRTS/PANTS as garments alone; pick a shirt; see/select its variants (same shirt, many materials); assign a new material variant via the chooser.
